answer: Each identity moors a pearl trap to an anchor under a bridge pier, locking a 70-credit bond. Catch is filed with anchor, pier, seal. An auditor recomputes the pearl count from pearl-growth table at that bridge pier. A shortfall over 10 percent, a moved anchor, or a reused seal burns the bond. First cost 34 credits; the kth fake pays 34 plus 6 times k minus 1, so the 1000th pays 6028 and 1000 fakes cost 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-trap ring fails: each seal binds one anchor, pier, key, so sharing triggers a double burn. An honest keeper pays 34 once, bond returned after audit.
